about: The main comparison document. The public page /compare/ (website/src/pages/compare.astro) is built from this file, so every fact is edited here and nowhere else. Each tool's 'checked' is the date its column was last read at the version named.

rows.title: An outside AI agent can be driven through it one step at a time
rows.ask: Can an assistant such as Claude or Cursor work through a workflow step by step, and be refused when it skips ahead or answers in the wrong shape?

verdict.text: Only Realm does this built in. The others give an outside agent, at most, tools that run a whole workflow.

realm.note: An MCP client calls execute_step for one step at a time. A step that is not eligible yet is refused, and when a step declares a schema, an answer that breaks it is refused.
realm.label: CODE + EXECUTED

langgraph.note: Agent Server exposes each graph as one MCP tool; one call runs the whole graph, with no sessions.
langgraph.label: DOCS

crewai.note: No MCP server in the open-source code; outside callers start a crew through A2A or the paid platform's API.
crewai.label: CODE + DOCS

mastra.note: MCPServer exposes a workflow as one tool, run_<key>, which runs the whole workflow.
mastra.label: CODE

maf.note: WorkflowMCPTool (alpha) runs a whole workflow, and refuses one that needs human input.
maf.label: CODE

temporal.note: Not built in. Temporal's own MCP server searches its docs; you can write a server whose tools start workflows.
temporal.label: DOCS + CODE

inngest.note: Its MCP server sends events, runs functions and reads traces. A client does not hand in step results through it.
inngest.label: DOCS + CODE

n8n.note: MCP execute_workflow runs a whole workflow, and does not support workflows with human-in-the-loop steps.
n8n.label: DOCS

dify.note: An app published as an MCP server is exactly one tool.
dify.label: CODE

rows.title: Decides which step runs next
rows.ask: Does the tool, not the model, decide the step order?

verdict.text: Level with the tools whose workflows are ordered by code, and the only one that holds an outside agent to that order. One gap: after a gate is answered, the next automatic step waits for an explicit call (#625).

realm.note: The engine works out the eligible steps after every result and refuses the others. Among several eligible steps, the caller picks. A guard step behind a gate is decided when the answer is written; an automatic step after a gate still waits for a call (#625, open).
realm.label: CODE + DOCS + EXECUTED

langgraph.note: The graph's edges decide; routing can use the model's output, but only to nodes the code wires in. Inside a prebuilt agent loop the model picks tools.
langgraph.label: DOCS

crewai.note: Sequential crews and Flows follow code; in hierarchical crews a manager LLM assigns the tasks.
crewai.label: DOCS

mastra.note: Workflows run a graph fixed in code; in agent networks a routing LLM picks the next agent.
mastra.label: DOCS

maf.note: Graph workflows run typed executors along edges; in group-chat, handoff and Magentic orchestrations an LLM picks who acts.
maf.label: DOCS + CODE

temporal.note: Your workflow code decides; when that code is an agent loop, the model picks the tools.
temporal.label: DOCS

inngest.note: Your code decides; in an agent loop "the model's response decides the next step".
inngest.label: DOCS

n8n.note: The graph sets node order; inside the AI Agent node the model picks tools, up to 10 iterations by default.
n8n.label: CODE + DOCS

dify.note: Workflow apps follow the graph; Agent nodes give the model control over tools.
dify.label: DOCS

rows.title: Checks the model's output against a schema
rows.ask: Is a step's output checked against a declared schema before the run moves on?

verdict.text: Level. Realm refuses a wrong-shape answer and lets the caller try again; n8n, CrewAI and LangChain's agent also send the error back to the model. In Realm the schema is optional per step.

realm.note: When a step declares a schema, a wrong-shape answer is refused before it is recorded; after 6 refusals the step fails, or uses a declared default. realm agent sends the error back to the model. Schemas are optional per step.
realm.label: CODE + DOCS + EXECUTED

langgraph.note: The graph does not check a node's output. LangChain's create_agent checks response_format and sends errors back to the model.
langgraph.label: DOCS

crewai.note: output_pydantic and guardrails check output and retry with the error up to 3 times; on the output_json path a failed conversion can let the run continue on raw text.
crewai.label: CODE + DOCS

mastra.note: An agent step's structured output is validated and fails the step by default; a plain step's output is not checked against its own schema.
mastra.label: CODE

maf.note: A Pydantic result is validated only when read; a dict schema is only parsed as JSON. No retry with errors found.
maf.label: CODE

temporal.note: Not checked by Temporal; your activity code validates, and failures become activity retries without the errors going back to the model.
temporal.label: CODE + DOCS

inngest.note: Model output and tool arguments are not checked; event data can be.
inngest.label: CODE

n8n.note: The Structured Output Parser checks the reply against a schema; Auto-Fix makes one more model call with the error, then fails.
n8n.label: CODE

dify.note: Only checks that the reply parses as JSON (repairing broken JSON); not checked against the schema.
dify.label: CODE

rows.title: Pauses for a person's decision, with a time limit
rows.ask: Is there a built-in step that waits for a person, and can it time out?

verdict.text: Level with n8n, Dify, Temporal and Inngest. Ahead of the frameworks that have no time limit. Realm's time limit is opt-in; by default a gate waits forever.

realm.note: A gate puts the run in gate_waiting and refuses later steps. A time limit is opt-in (abort or a default answer on expiry); by default it waits forever.
realm.label: DOCS + EXECUTED

langgraph.note: interrupt() pauses inside a node and resume continues it. No time limit on the wait.
langgraph.label: CODE + DOCS

crewai.note: Open source: console input or Flow feedback, no time limit. The paid platform adds email review with a timeout.
crewai.label: CODE + DOCS

mastra.note: A step can suspend and be resumed with data. No time limit found.
mastra.label: DOCS

maf.note: request_info() pauses and routes the answer back by id. No time limit in core.
maf.label: CODE

temporal.note: Wait for a Signal with a timeout.
temporal.label: DOCS

inngest.note: step.waitForEvent with a timeout, which returns null on expiry.
inngest.label: DOCS

n8n.note: Send and Wait (approval, text or form), with an optional wait limit; when the limit passes, the run continues.
n8n.label: CODE + DOCS

dify.note: A Human Input node with a form, action buttons and a timeout branch (3 days by default in the editor).
dify.label: CODE + DOCS

rows.title: Records who made the decision, and checks it
rows.ask: Is the person who answered recorded, and is their identity checked?

verdict.text: Behind n8n's Slack and Telegram approvals, which can restrict who may approve and record who clicked; Dify, which records the account that answered on its web app and gives each recipient its own token; and CrewAI's paid platform, which checks the reviewer's email (per its docs). Realm records a name the caller states and checks nothing; in a test the agent approved its own gate, and the proof token, which shows only the conversation, recorded it as matched.

realm.note: Records a name the caller states and checks nothing. Each answer also records whether it passed back the token from the reply that opened the gate, which proves the conversation, not the person: in a test the MCP agent approved its own gate, passed its token, and was recorded as matched. Slack records no name (#603).
realm.label: DOCS + CODE + EXECUTED

langgraph.note: resume carries no field for who answered. Agent Server's auth can check the caller if you write that code.
langgraph.label: CODE + DOCS

crewai.note: Open source: no answerer recorded, and the answer itself is kept only on the running flow unless your code copies it into the flow's state. Paid platform: the reviewer's identity is recorded and checked against a signed token (docs only).
crewai.label: CODE + DOCS + INFERRED

mastra.note: The step result has no field for who resumed it; a permission check needs the enterprise edition. Its chat channels' tool-call approvals accept only the person who asked, and record no approver.
mastra.label: CODE

maf.note: No responder field; authentication is left to your code.
maf.label: DOCS

temporal.note: The approver is a field you put in the signal; the event also stores an identity string the sender sets. Since server 1.32 an opt-in setting adds a principal the server checks to each event; it is off by default.
temporal.source: api history/v1/message.proto:618-635; server v1.32.0 mutable_state_impl.go:7694-7713, dynamicconfig/constants.go:930-935
temporal.label: CODE + DOCS

inngest.note: Only what your code puts in the event; anyone with the environment's event key can send one.
inngest.label: DOCS

n8n.note: When turned on, Slack and Telegram approvals restrict who may approve: a click from anyone not listed is refused and the run keeps waiting, and the answer records who clicked (id, name, source), on a callback n8n checks came from Slack or Telegram. Its other channels send a signed link that anyone holding it can answer, recorded as {approved, respondedAt} only.
n8n.label: CODE

dify.note: Records the submitting user and recipient; each recipient gets a token. Email links: anyone with the link can answer. Through its API, the answering user is a name the caller sends, and deleting a conversation deletes its answers.
dify.label: CODE + DOCS

rows.title: Records each step's input and output
rows.ask: Is each step's input and output kept, and for how long?

verdict.text: Level. Realm keeps records until you delete them, as do the tools that store their own (LangGraph, Mastra, Microsoft Agent Framework, Dify). n8n prunes after 14 days by default, Inngest Cloud keeps traces 24 hours to 14 days below Enterprise, and Temporal Cloud keeps history 1 to 90 days.

realm.note: Each step's input, output and timing; the program that took it (stated or from the OS user, not verified); every gate answer with its stated answerer; why a step was skipped and why the run ended. Under realm agent, the token counts the provider reported. Kept until purged; one-file export.
realm.label: DOCS + EXECUTED

langgraph.note: A state snapshot at every step plus each node's writes, with a persistent checkpointer. No export file.
langgraph.label: DOCS

crewai.note: Task inputs and outputs of the latest run only; full checkpoints are opt-in.
crewai.label: CODE

mastra.note: Each step's input, output and timestamps in the run snapshot, with persistent storage.
mastra.label: CODE

maf.note: A chain of checkpoints with messages and state.
maf.label: CODE

temporal.note: The event history keeps inputs and results; Temporal Cloud keeps it 1 to 90 days, then you export.
temporal.label: DOCS

inngest.note: Step results and a trace per run. Inngest Cloud keeps trace history 24 hours (Free), 7 days (Pro), 14 days (Business) or up to 365 days (Enterprise); self-hosted Inngest does not remove them.
inngest.label: DOCS

n8n.note: Each node's input and output with the execution; pruned after 14 days or 10,000 executions by default.
n8n.label: CODE + DOCS

dify.note: Every node execution's inputs and outputs; kept indefinitely on self-host by default.
dify.label: CODE

rows.title: Shows if a record was changed afterwards
rows.ask: Is the record hashed, chained or signed so an edit can be detected?

verdict.text: None of the tools here does this. LangGraph's optional encryption hides values but does not show that a record was changed.

realm.note: A SHA-256 hash of each output, never re-checked. In a test, hand edits to an agent's output, a person's choice and the answerer's name all showed as real, with no warning; nothing is signed and there is no verify command.
realm.label: CODE + DOCS + EXECUTED

langgraph.note: Optional encryption hides values but does not show tampering: a value stored as plain text, or encrypted text copied from another record, still loads; on Postgres, plain values and metadata are never encrypted; a deleted or reordered checkpoint goes unnoticed.
langgraph.label: CODE + INFERRED

crewai.note: No hashing or signing in the open-source code. The paid platform claims immutable audit logs for reviews (not checked).
crewai.label: CODE

mastra.note: No hash or signature on step records.
mastra.label: CODE

maf.note: The only hash fingerprints the graph's shape; the docs call checkpoint storage a trust boundary.
maf.label: CODE + DOCS

temporal.note: No hashing or signing of the history; the same permission that sends a signal can delete a history.
temporal.source: llms-full.txt grep; cli commands.yaml:4767; common/api/metadata.go:111-115 (server v1.32.0)
temporal.label: DOCS + CODE

inngest.note: No hashing or signing; Inngest itself never edits a stored event, but whoever has the database can.
inngest.label: CODE

n8n.note: No hashing or signing of execution data.
n8n.label: CODE

dify.note: Archive bundles carry MD5 checksums against corruption only.
dify.label: CODE

rows.title: Carries on after a crash, by itself
rows.ask: If the process dies mid-run, does the run resume without a person or your code stepping in?

verdict.text: Behind Temporal, Inngest and Mastra, which resume a run on their own. LangGraph, CrewAI and Microsoft Agent Framework resume when your code calls them. A Realm run survives on disk, but a person or a driver restarts it, and a crash during an agent step needs a manual reclaim that may repeat the step's work.

realm.note: State is saved after every step, but nothing resumes it: someone starts a driver again. Claims now name a holder and a time, but nothing checks that the holder is alive. A crash mid agent step needs realm run reclaim --force, which may repeat the work. No fsync.
realm.label: CODE + DOCS

langgraph.note: With a persistent checkpointer, a run resumes from the last checkpoint when your code calls it again with the same thread_id; finished nodes are not re-run.
langgraph.label: DOCS

crewai.note: Opt-in checkpoints; a run resumes when your code restores it (completed tasks are skipped). Writes are best-effort.
crewai.label: DOCS

mastra.note: With persistent storage, active runs restart from the last active step.
mastra.label: DOCS

maf.note: Restarts from a checkpoint your code chooses; resuming is not automatic in core. The durable extension makes it automatic.
maf.label: DOCS

temporal.note: Replays the event history and resumes from the point of failure.
temporal.label: DOCS

inngest.note: Saves each step's result and retries from the step that failed.
inngest.label: DOCS

n8n.note: Waits survive a restart; an execution running at the crash is marked crashed, not resumed.
n8n.label: CODE

dify.note: Paused runs resume; no resume of a run that crashed mid-node was found.
dify.label: CODE + INFERRED

rows.title: Can be used as an MCP server
rows.ask: Can an MCP client (Claude, Cursor, …) connect to it?

verdict.text: Level: n8n, Dify, Mastra and Inngest have one too, and LangGraph and Microsoft's in part. What only Realm does is the first row: its tools work one step at a time, where the others run whole workflows. CrewAI has no MCP server; Temporal's own MCP server searches its docs and runs no workflows.

realm.note: 10 tools over stdio (realm mcp) or HTTP (realm serve), at step level. realm serve checks one shared token.
realm.label: CODE + EXECUTED

langgraph.note: Only in Agent Server (Elastic-2.0, needs Postgres and Redis); one tool per graph.
langgraph.label: DOCS

crewai.note: No MCP server in the open-source code.
crewai.label: CODE

mastra.note: Agents, tools and workflows over stdio and HTTP; a workflow is one whole-run tool.
mastra.label: DOCS + CODE

maf.note: An agent or a workflow as one tool; the workflow tool is alpha.
maf.label: CODE

temporal.note: Its MCP server searches the docs; nothing built in for running workflows.
temporal.label: DOCS

inngest.note: Cloud and local servers for operations: send events, run functions, read traces.
inngest.label: DOCS + CODE

n8n.note: Per-workflow tools and an instance server that can also build workflows; not stdio.
n8n.label: DOCS

dify.note: An app as one tool, off by default; credentials in the URL.
dify.label: DOCS

rows.title: Steps can call other MCP servers as tools
rows.ask: Can a step use tools from other MCP servers?

verdict.text: Behind. Realm supports stdio servers only, and only when realm agent drives the step.

realm.note: stdio servers only, and only when realm agent drives the step.
realm.label: DOCS

mastra.note: MCPClient over stdio and Streamable HTTP.
mastra.label: DOCS

temporal.note: Through agent-framework integrations; each MCP call runs as an activity.
temporal.label: DOCS

inngest.note: AgentKit agents take MCP servers over HTTP, SSE or WS.
inngest.label: DOCS

dify.note: MCP servers as tool providers, HTTP only.
dify.label: DOCS

rows.title: Keeps what the prompt cache did on each model call
rows.ask: Does a run's record keep, for each model call, how much of the prompt the provider read from its cache and how much it wrote to it? Realm's answer is for 0.46.0, the version in its column head. The other tools' answers to this question were read from each tool's code on 2026-10-09, at its default branch and not at the version in its column head; each source names the commit.

verdict.text: Level with LangGraph, whose checkpoints save each model message whole, cache counts included. Mastra, Microsoft Agent Framework, Temporal, Inngest and CrewAI keep part of it: per step, summed, or without the 5-minute/1-hour split. n8n and Dify keep no cache counts in a stored run. Realm keeps one entry per model call, and a count the provider did not report is left out, never written as 0.

realm.note: For each model call realm agent makes for a step, the step's record holds one entry: the whole prompt size, the part read from the cache, the part written to it (with the 5-minute/1-hour split of the writes where the provider gives it) and the output tokens. A schema-repair call is an entry of its own. A figure the provider did not report is absent, never counted as 0.
realm.label: CODE + DOCS

langgraph.note: A model message kept in the graph's state is saved whole in the checkpoint, so the cache counts the provider put on it are saved with it. This follows from how checkpoints store messages; it is not a cache feature.
langgraph.label: CODE

crewai.note: Counts of cached prompt tokens and of tokens written to the cache are summed per run, with the cached tokens folded into the prompt-token count. There is no entry per model call; whether a stored record keeps the sums was not read.
crewai.label: CODE + DOCS

mastra.note: The durable agent keeps each iteration's usage and a running total of cached-input and cache-creation tokens in its saved iteration state. Only the durable agent was read, not Mastra's other workflows.
mastra.label: CODE

maf.note: Its usage details hold the tokens read from and written to a provider cache, with no 5-minute/1-hour split. Whether a saved run keeps them for each model call was not read.
maf.label: CODE

temporal.note: No cache feature of its own. In the TypeScript AI SDK integration each model call runs as an activity whose result carries the cache read and write counts, so the event history should hold them; the stored payload was not read.
temporal.label: CODE + INFERRED

inngest.note: Telemetry attributes set inside a step are summed into the step's metadata, cache reads and writes included: one sum per step, not one entry per model call. For writes it reads only the deprecated attribute name.
inngest.label: CODE

n8n.note: A workflow run's token usage holds input and output tokens only, and the Anthropic node adds cache reads and writes into the input count. The Agents product keeps tokens and a cost per run, with no cache columns. Instance AI's per-step cache view sits in an in-memory debug buffer, not in a stored record.
n8n.source: metadata-utils.ts:26-37; message.operation.ts:386-394; CreateAgentExecutionTables.ts:44-64; run-debug-buffer.ts:187-195 @ n8n 9ff8d4fc, read 2026-10-09
n8n.label: CODE

dify.note: The run record's usage object has no cache field. The Anthropic plugin folds cache reads and writes into a price-weighted prompt-token count instead, so the counts are not in the record.
dify.label: CODE

rows.title: Prices cache reads and writes in a run's cost
rows.ask: Does a run's cost price the tokens read from the prompt cache and the tokens written to it at their own rates, not as plain input? Realm's answer is for 0.48.0, which is newer than the 0.46.0 in its column head; the other Realm answers on this page are for 0.46.0. The other tools' answers to this question were read from each tool's code on 2026-10-09, at its default branch and not at the version in its column head; each source names the commit.

verdict.text: Level with Mastra, which prices cache reads and each write size at their own rates. n8n's Agents product and Dify's Anthropic plugin price them too, each in a narrower way. CrewAI, LangGraph, Temporal, Microsoft Agent Framework and Inngest price nothing that we found. In Realm 0.48.0 the figure is worked out when a run is read, names its price source, and says what caching saved or cost against no caching; we found no other tool among these eight that works out that last figure.

realm.note: In 0.48.0, not the 0.46.0 of this column. When a run is read, each model call is priced at its own cache read and write rates, from your economics file or an installed price list; Realm ships no prices. The figure names its price source, says call-date or current price, and says what caching saved or cost against no caching. A call it cannot price is counted out and the figure starts with ≥. We found no other of these eight that works out that net (searched 2026-10-09).
realm.source: step-view.ts:769; price-source.ts:30, :163; cache-economics.ts:186, :244; inspect.ts:799-805; cache-economics.md:129-131; CHANGELOG 0.48.0 (all at v0.48.0)
realm.label: CODE + DOCS + INFERRED

langgraph.note: We found no price calculation in LangGraph's own code: a search for price and cost terms came back empty. Cost tracking in LangChain's own packages was not read.
langgraph.source: grep for price and cost terms in langgraph and langgraphjs, read 2026-10-09
langgraph.label: INFERRED

crewai.note: Cache token counts are kept, but we found no price calculated from them: the two hits for price and cost terms were read and are not cost calculation.
crewai.source: types/usage_metrics.py; grep for price and cost terms in crewAI @ 140bfcb8, read 2026-10-09
crewai.label: CODE + INFERRED

mastra.note: Mastra's observability prices at ingest from an embedded price snapshot, with separate meters for cache reads, 5-minute writes and 1-hour writes. A failed price lookup is recorded as a costing error. It does not say what caching saved.
mastra.label: CODE + INFERRED

maf.note: Cache counts are kept, but we found no price calculated from them: the hits for price and cost terms were read and are not LLM cost calculation.
maf.source: grep for price and cost terms in agent-framework @ fd52de71, read 2026-10-09
maf.label: INFERRED

temporal.note: We found no price calculation in the SDKs or the AI integrations: a search for price and cost terms came back empty.
temporal.source: grep for price and cost terms in sdk-typescript, sdk-python, ai-integrations, read 2026-10-09
temporal.label: INFERRED

inngest.note: We found no price calculation: the two hits for price and cost terms in inngest-js were read and are not cost calculation; agent-kit had none.
inngest.source: grep for price and cost terms in inngest-js @ a00d53fe and agent-kit, read 2026-10-09
inngest.label: INFERRED

n8n.note: The Agents product prices a call at the time it is made, from a price catalog it fetches live, with cache reads and writes at their own rates and a 1-hour write scaled when 1 hour was asked. It stores one cost per run. The workflow nodes keep only input and output tokens, with the cache folded into the input count.
n8n.source: agents catalog.ts:295-351; CreateAgentExecutionTables.ts:44-64; metadata-utils.ts:26-37 @ n8n 9ff8d4fc, read 2026-10-09
n8n.label: CODE

dify.note: The Anthropic plugin turns cache reads and writes into a price-weighted prompt-token count, with multipliers written in its code, and prices that count at the time of the call from its bundled price file. The counts themselves are not kept.
dify.label: CODE

cells.crewai: Python + JSONC/YAML; visual editor on the paid platform
cells.n8n: Visual editor (JSON); code nodes; TS SDK

cells.realm: CLI, MCP, library, webhooks. No UI
cells.crewai: CLI, SDK, platform UI and API
cells.mastra: CLI, SDK, API, Studio UI, cloud

cells.realm: Self-hosted; JSON files on one machine
cells.langgraph: Both; SQLite, Postgres, MongoDB (server: Postgres + Redis)
cells.dify: Both; Postgres, Redis, a vector store

realm.stronger: Drives an outside agent step by step and refuses out-of-order steps and wrong-shape answers; works with any MCP client and no model key; records why each step was skipped and why the run ended, which program took each step, and each gate answer; refuses a misspelt trust level or an invalid schema when the workflow is loaded.
realm.weaker: No UI: no visual editor or dashboard; no loops: a workflow cannot go back to an earlier step, repeat a step until a condition holds, or run a step once per item of a list (only a retry of the same step, or a separate run per item); runs are stored as JSON files on one machine; nothing resumes a run after a crash; a gate records the name the answerer gives and checks nothing; after a gate is answered, the next automatic step waits for a call; agent steps can use tools only from local (stdio) MCP servers, and only under realm agent.

langgraph.stronger: Time travel and forking from any checkpoint; per-node retries, timeouts and caching; Postgres and MongoDB with encryption; Studio debugger; LangSmith tracing; Python and JS.
langgraph.weaker: The graph does not check a node's output; interrupts have no time limit and no answerer; the MCP server needs the licensed Agent Server and runs whole graphs.

crewai.stronger: Role-based multi-agent crews; memory and knowledge; A2A; a large tool catalogue; on the paid platform, email review with the reviewer checked.
crewai.weaker: A manager LLM can decide the order; output_json can continue unvalidated; open-source reviews record no one and have no time limit; no MCP server.

mastra.stronger: One TypeScript stack for agents, memory, RAG and evals; about 20 storage backends; Studio with time travel; scheduled workflows; MCP on the latest spec.
mastra.weaker: An outside agent can only start a whole workflow; no answerer on human steps and no time limit; a plain step's output is not checked.

maf.stronger: Python, C# and Go; ready-made multi-agent patterns; workflow types checked when built; durable execution through Azure; A2A hosting.
maf.weaker: A dict schema is never checked; human steps record no responder and have no time limit; the MCP workflow tool is alpha.

temporal.stronger: Production record since 2020; crash recovery by design; 8 SDKs; Signals, Updates and Schedules; Cloud with high-availability tiers; integrations with 10+ agent frameworks.
temporal.weaker: Your code is the agent loop and the checks; approver identity is up to you; Cloud keeps history at most 90 days unless exported.

inngest.stronger: Event-driven runs; concurrency, throttling and debounce; hosted model calls; realtime streaming; evals; serverless-friendly.
inngest.weaker: Model output is not checked; approvals carry only what the event says; traces last 24 hours to 14 days below Enterprise.

n8n.stronger: 1,500+ integrations by its README (the repository description says 400+) and 9,000+ templates; human review of AI tool calls on 9 channels; visual editor; MCP server that can build workflows; queue mode.
n8n.weaker: Inside the agent node the model decides; link approvals record no one; records pruned after 14 days by default; not OSI open source.

dify.stronger: A rich human-input node that records the answerer and has a timeout branch; RAG pipelines; hundreds of model providers; logs kept by default.
dify.weaker: Structured output is only parsed, not checked; an MCP client runs a whole app; email approval links work for anyone holding them.
